entries.topic: Investigation of intermittent Agent support-log uploads
facts: One provided local log from an affected Agent records 22 deferred uploads and one acknowledged success during 13 October 2026, approximately 13:30 to 19:52.
Failures consist of 14 timeouts, five keep-alive closures and three unexpected receive closures.
Agent source enforces 10-second request/read-write timeout; the shared gateway source permits a lock wait up to 15 seconds before archive operations.
Agent upload backoff escalates from one minute to 30 minutes; a manual sealed entry does not prove completed upload.
The Agent was upgraded during the trace and upload failures continued. Available evidence does not prove the same root cause on the second affected Agent.
alternatives: Preserve local pending logs and inspect one other affected Agent for comparison.
Prepare Agent-only change proposal: aligned bounded timeout, serialized upload attempts, safer connection recovery, visible upload status and reliable manual retry.
Investigate gateway contention separately before considering changes to its runtime.

entries.topic: Compare second affected Windows Agent support-log file to first
facts: Owner supplied a second local Agent diagnostic file from another affected workstation. Across 13 October local observations, first Agent has 7,663 lines, 22 GOOGLE_APPS_SCRIPT upload=DEFER (14 timeout, 5 keep-alive connection closed, 3 unexpected receive errors) and one Drive-confirmed upload=PASS; second Agent has 1,983 lines, 20 upload=DEFER (16 timeout, 4 keep-alive closure) and one Drive-confirmed upload=PASS.

Second Agent log spans roughly 13:38 to 20:10 VN; only confirmed Drive upload at 15:18:40, with 15 subsequent failed uploads through 20:09:36. First Agent shows one pass at 13:35:36 and 20 later deferred events through 19:48:57.
Both affected machines ran v130 after local restarts; second logs v125 before changing to v130 at 15:18. Repeated v130 starts on second machine were observed but their cause is not established.

Second Agent manual=SEALED upload=TRY at 20:09:46 followed 20:09:36 timeout by ten seconds and falls inside retry_after 20:39:36 VN; thus that marker is not upload confirmation and existing cooldown can defer manual transmission.

Second Agent performs Firebase refresh PASS and Firestore Confirm poll PASS in same period. This is selective degraded support-log route, not proven total Internet outage or inability to authenticate.

Current Agent source uses request Timeout=10000 ms and ReadWriteTimeout=10000 ms for Gateway HTTP POST, backoff up to 30 minutes and no explicit single-flight gate; gateway source uses waitLock(15000) plus Worker/Drive operations. This is a design mismatch and plausible latency mechanism; shared Apps Script lock delay is not established as actual event cause without execution traces.

Second trace shows three close-together failures at 15:20:43, 15:20:49.136 and 15:20:49.408, motivating verification of concurrent in-flight flush and retry fencing; timing alone does not prove an upload race.
Scope note: original raw user logs remain private and are not committed; only aggregate counts and sanitized aliases are recorded.
alternatives: Measure first, read-only: compare existing Gateway execution durations, completion/Drive receipts and network/proxy behavior for the same time periods; verify local pending count and oldest pending age on both affected agents.

Preferred Owner-reviewed Agent-only fix: serialized log uploads, response-safe timeout and connection handling, bounded backoff/manual retry semantics, unambiguous confirmed-status UI and persisted pending bundles.
Gateway optimization only if measured lock/Worker/Drive execution time implicates backend; no added polling/provider writes or unrelated business modifications.

entries.topic: Scheduled D167 19h SKU DELTA failed to reach confirmed upload; 11-second retry-storm bypasses 15-minute cooldown

entries.topic: Owner asks Office-versus-PDA network check for SKU automatic update and backlog record
facts: Owner requests backlog checkpoint and specific assessment whether automatic SKU update uses corporate Office Wi-Fi or requires ordinary/PDA Internet; no code or deployment instruction was provided.

Current Windows Agent code does not bind D167 requests to a Wi-Fi SSID or select a forced network adapter. Agent reads WMS XLSX via allowlisted HTTPS GET with Windows system proxy, and sends schedule/stage/publish through a registered script.google.com Agent Operations Gateway. Apps Script uses UrlFetchApp to reach Beta Worker, so it can operate with an Office allowlisted Google endpoint without direct Office-to-Cloudflare connection.

Google Apps Script HTTPS endpoint is an external Google service, not a private LAN peer; the WMS/source and upload/Worker legs have distinct network access requirements. Actual Office path is subject to company firewall/proxy and Google quota.

Privacy-sanitized local diagnostic: Agent A saw Office Wi-Fi at 17:45 and 18:54 with D167_SKU sync=DEFER events nearby, and Firebase token refresh PASS from Office at 18:54; at 19:51 it saw PDA Wi-Fi. Agent B had earlier Office sightings, but at 15:18 (preceding repeated SKU errors) it was using PDA Wi-Fi. Therefore Office is not the sole failing network, and Office Firebase success is not proof of Office SKU upload success.

Neither attached local log contains DELTA_19 stage=DONE or Service receipt. Logs do not attach the effective interface, corporate proxy response or URLFetch response to each SKU attempt. 19:00 interface and complete Office-based update remain unverified; repeated failures and UrlFetch quota are already captured in D168-REQ-009.

Local logs contain Wi-Fi names in some diagnostic entries, a privacy/observability gap against the existing logging spec prohibition on SSID/BSSID. Do not commit or expose raw values; prefer bounded network-class labels if instrumentation is later approved.
alternatives: No source change: obtain read-only Gateway status and Service receipt on known Office-only connection, compare to PDA and inspect existing Apps Script execution logs safely.

Preferred conditional future Agent fix: preserve existing Office-compatible Apps Script route, fix D168-REQ-009 retry-storm/diagnostic gaps without extra provider polling, then one controlled field test with durable receipt.
If corporate filtering blocks the registered Google Gateway, fail closed and request an approved corporate endpoint solution; do not silently bypass filtering or create an unauthorized transport.

entries.topic: Office can reach SUPRA WMS but cannot directly reach Cloudflare; choose Office-capable SKU uplink using existing Google transport
facts: Owner confirms company Office network cannot connect Cloudflare directly and WMS SUPRA report data is reachable via Office with the previously tested Bin Inventory XLSX access protocol. User asks for a viable Office-to-Service upload architecture.

Existing D167 already implements this split: WMS read-only XLSX GET over Office using the current managed Agent browser and Windows system proxy; SKU normalized/fingerprinted locally; Agent HTTPS post to script.google.com Apps Script Gateway; Apps Script calls inventory-beta Worker via UrlFetchApp, and InventoryCore owns transactional SKU persistence/atomic DONE.

Agent-to-Service SKU uplink is not direct Office-to-Cloudflare and must not transmit WMS authorization/session material or unparsed XLSX to the gateway. Existing Gateway does token verification and Worker forwarding, each consuming UrlFetch; the Agent sends 500-SKU stages, up to 10 for 5000 SKU.

Google officially confirms Apps Script ContentService JSON output redirects to script.googleusercontent.com; Office may permit script.google.com yet block the redirect. Source Agent AllowAutoRedirect=true but actual Office firewall/proxy permission is not field-proven.

Two Agent logs show recurring failed requests and quota-related Usage errors, while one-second readiness retry triggers can bypass SKU scheduler 15min cooldown. Thus apparent Office failure cannot be attributed uniquely to direct Cloudflare blocking; Apps Script quota and redirected response need independent inspection.

Existing D090 authority excludes Office direct Cloudflare and Firebase RTDB as Office carrier; Firestore was field-proven as an Office candidate for confirmation. This does not automatically establish an SKU Firestore-to-Worker bridge or authorize a new integration.
